original_test_intent: Trigger the Intel Three-Strike timeout at each approved socket/port, confirm the expected catastrophic crash/hang and automatic recovery path, and correlate CPU/UPI fatal evidence across BMC, UEFI, OS and physical indicators.
original_method: On a dedicated SUT, an FAE/operator enables the exact EDKII controls, validates the socket/port, performs one approved Three-Strike injection and starts an independent timeline. The operator waits the specified autonomous-reboot interval, avoids premature power intervention, then follows the vendor recovery boundary, collects BMC/UEFI/OS and front-panel/LCD artifacts and restores settings.
manual_activity: A qualified FAE/operator must configure BIOS, identify the port, authorize and trigger the intentional outage, observe indicators, wait the protected recovery interval and perform any permitted recovery/restoration.
required_inputs: Supported platform/CPU/socket-port mapping and Intel ITP/CScripts build/hash
Approved injectThreeStrike semantics and exact catastrophic signatures
Maximum crash/hang and automatic-reboot windows plus independent console/power timeline
Front-panel/LCD applicability and reason CPU Over Temp represents this stimulus
Vendor recovery, post-recovery health and BIOS restoration procedure
safety_requirements: Dedicated idle SUT, stable power, independent console and explicit intentional-crash approval
Preserve baseline logs; do not clear the only pre-event evidence
One verified target and injection only; no automatic retry
Do not power-cycle inside the approved autonomous-recovery window
Abort/escalate on wrong target, power/thermal anomaly, exceeded timeout or unrecoverable boot
agent_execution_scope: Capture approved non-mutating baseline and post-recovery artifacts when the SUT is available
Do not enable BIOS settings, run the injector, decide when to power-cycle/reset, repeat the fault or declare PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Approve tool, target, signatures and intentional crash
Define exact hang/reboot timers and permitted recovery transitions
Explain or correct the LCD CPU Over Temp expectation and required front-panel behavior
Approve restoration/health checks and final verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The SSH grep is partial post-event evidence and may be unreachable during the intended crash; it cannot prove the Three-Strike command, reboot window, UEFI record or indicators and disables host verification.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Only the exact FAE-operated `ei.injectThreeStrike(socket,port)` may stimulate the fault; agent collection is read-only and must tolerate the expected outage without initiating recovery.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Socket 0~N, command, listed BIOS paths and 30/10-minute estimates are preserved; no port or reboot limit is guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use an external timestamp/console monitor, record the exact injection transcript, BMC event stream and power state through the outage, wait an approved timer, capture recovered UEFI/OS evidence and indicators, then diff/restore BIOS settings and verify health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds bounded timing and recovery without weakening the expected crash/hang/reboot behavior.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A log tail after recovery cannot prove when or why the system hung, whether reboot was autonomous, or whether physical criteria matched.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The action intentionally removes service and may leave the system hung, unbootable or with persistent RAS/debug state.

project_override_considerations: The package/user-confirmation class allows a controlled future run, not autonomous outage creation. Missing approvals or recovery paths produce BLOCKED execution, never a DUT verdict.
expected_evidence: Owner/FAE approval, SUT/CPU/socket/firmware identity and target map
Harness hash, exact command transcript and synchronized crash/hang/reboot timeline
BMC catastrophic event, recovered UEFI UPI-fatal entry and approved OS/console evidence
BIOS restoration, post-recovery health and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: `Reboot eventually` has no maximum or permitted recovery action, so timeout versus expected hang is undecidable. The LCD CPU Over Temp message is not explained as the expected Three-Strike/UPI indication and may represent a different fault.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The named Intel command and intended catastrophic behavior are concrete enough for conditional execution once tool, target, timers, oracle, recovery and operator controls are approved.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 9 Wistron-System RAS-00729-V003: approve platform/socket-port mapping, Intel ITP/CScripts version/hash and `injectThreeStrike` semantics; define expected crash/hang and maximum autonomous-reboot intervals, forbidden/permitted power recovery and BIOS restoration; specify exact BMC/UEFI/OS and front-panel signatures; and explain or correct why an LCD CPU Over Temp message is required for the Three-Strike/UPI event.

review_improvement: This review converts `eventually` into an explicit engineering timing decision and prevents recovery action or a thermally worded LCD message from being silently treated as correct Three-Strike behavior.
independent_technical_reasoning: Three-Strike is distinguished by a catastrophic timeout path whose service interruption is expected, so availability of SSH after injection is not a safe control or primary oracle. The test must separate autonomous reboot from operator recovery with an external timeline and maximum wait; otherwise both an immediate manual reset and an indefinite hang could be misreported as success. A CPU-over-temperature display is not self-evidently caused by a UPI timeout and needs a platform event-map justification. Exact FAE tooling and human control make the case conditionally executable, while the agent must never initiate or repeat the outage.
